clusterName.description: Name of the Kubernetes cluster. Used as the prefix for every bare-metal host this blueprint renders, so it must be a valid DNS-1123 label.
clusterName.title: Cluster name

k8sVersion.description: Version of Kubernetes to install, as published by pkgs.k8s.io -- for example v1.36.6. Drives the kubeadm, kubelet and kubectl package version on every node, so it must be a version that repository actually carries. Upstream Kubernetes is installed unmodified.
k8sVersion.title: Kubernetes version

install.title: CNI plugin
install.description: Set to `cilium` to install Cilium with Helm -- the default, and the only value with a supported path. Any other value applies the manifest at `manifestUrl` with kubectl instead, which is how you bring your own CNI.

manifestUrl.title: CNI manifest URL
manifestUrl.description: Manifest applied with kubectl when `install` is not `cilium`. Note that a CNI without NetworkPolicy support -- Flannel, for one -- gives you a cluster that cannot express which pods may not talk to which.

version.description: Cilium chart version to install. Pin a stable release: a pre-release under hardware that takes a wipe-and-redeploy cycle to recover is not worth the risk.
version.title: Cilium version

helmVersion.description: Version of the Helm binary fetched onto the first control plane node, which has no Helm package of its own. Only used by the Cilium path.
helmVersion.title: Helm version

kubeProxyReplacement.title: Replace kube-proxy with Cilium
kubeProxyReplacement.description: Let Cilium's eBPF implementation replace kube-proxy, which is then never installed rather than installed and removed. Leave on unless you have a specific reason not to: with it off, nothing implements hostPort, which fails the CNCF conformance suite's HostPort test, and Service type=LoadBalancer is unavailable because Cilium's LB-IPAM and L2 announcements both require it. Only applies to the Cilium path.

cni.title: Pod network (CNI)
cni.description: Which pod network to install once the first control plane is up.

podCIDR.title: Pod CIDR
podCIDR.description: Address range pods are allocated from. Must not overlap the Service CIDR or anything routable on the blades' own network.

serviceCIDR.title: Service CIDR
serviceCIDR.description: Address range ClusterIP Services are allocated from. Must not overlap the pod CIDR.

managementApiReachability.description: How the blades reach the management cluster's API server -- an external load balancer, kube-vip, MetalLB, or a NodePort with DNS. Recorded for operators and for later milestones; it does not itself configure anything.
managementApiReachability.title: Management API reachability

network.title: Cluster networking
network.description: Pod and Service address ranges, and how the blades reach the management cluster.

source.title: Image URL
source.description: URL of the OS image, reachable from the Ironic conductor. Every node in the cluster is deployed from this one image.

checksum.title: Image checksum
checksum.description: Checksum of the image, or the URL of a checksum file. Ironic verifies the image against it before writing it to disk.

image.title: Operating system image
image.description: The OS image written to every blade in this cluster. Must be cloud-init enabled and Debian- or Ubuntu-shaped, because the generated first-boot configuration uses apt.

lifecycleNamespace.title: Host namespace
lifecycleNamespace.description: Namespace the bare-metal host resources are created in. Defaults to the namespace of the cluster composition itself.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the Ironic endpoint configuration resource.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Namespace of the Ironic endpoint configuration resource.

configurationRef.title: Ironic endpoint reference
configurationRef.description: The resource holding the Ironic API endpoint and credentials used to provision this cluster's blades.

ironicAuth.description: Credentials baked into each control plane's first-boot configuration so the node can publish its own join token back to Ironic. This is the rendezvous path for networks where a blade can reach Ironic but not the management cluster's API server.

authUrl.title: Keystone URL
authUrl.description: Keystone identity endpoint, as reachable from the blades -- for example http://192.0.2.1:5000.

ironicUrl.title: Ironic API URL
ironicUrl.description: Ironic bare-metal API endpoint, as reachable from the blades -- for example http://192.0.2.1:6385. This is the endpoint the blades actually use.

username.title: Keystone username
username.description: Keystone user the blades authenticate as. A user scoped to just the one project, with the member role, is enough -- updating a node's extra fields needs no administrator.

password.title: Keystone password
password.description: Password for that user. It is written into each control plane's first-boot configuration in plain text and is readable by anyone who can read the rendered host resource, so use a dedicated credential and rotate it rather than reusing an administrator's.

userDomain.title: Keystone user domain
userDomain.description: Identity domain the user belongs to. `Default` unless your deployment says otherwise.

ironicAuth.title: Ironic credentials for the blades

managementCluster.description: How a blade talks back to the management cluster that runs Krateo. Only needed when the join token is published through the Kubernetes API rather than through Ironic.

caBundle.title: API server CA bundle
caBundle.description: CA certificate for the management cluster's API server. Optional: the blueprint reads the cluster's own published root CA. Set it only where that publisher is disabled.

serviceAccountNamespace.title: Service account namespace
serviceAccountNamespace.description: Namespace for the service account a control plane uses to publish its join token. Defaults to the namespace of the cluster composition.

managementCluster.title: Management cluster access

endpoint.description: Stable address clients and joining nodes use to reach the API server. Required for a multi-node control plane, where it must be a load-balanced virtual address rather than any one node. Leave empty for a single node, which advertises its own address.
endpoint.title: API server endpoint

etcd.description: etcd for a multi-node control plane, run as a service on each control plane node independently of kubeadm's stacked etcd. A single-node control plane ignores this and uses stacked etcd, which has no member dance to go wrong.

aptPackage.title: etcd package
aptPackage.description: apt package and version installed on the control plane nodes, for example etcd-server=3.5.16-4. Any etcd 3.x speaks the same gRPC API to the API server.

snapshotImage.title: etcdctl image
snapshotImage.description: Container image providing etcdctl for the snapshot job. Match it to the etcd minor version installed on the nodes.

snapshotSchedule.title: Snapshot schedule
snapshotSchedule.description: Cron schedule for etcd snapshots. Defaults to every six hours.

snapshotRetentionDays.title: Snapshot retention (days)
snapshotRetentionDays.description: How many days of snapshots to keep on the node before older ones are deleted.

etcd.title: etcd

nodes.description: The control plane members, in order. The first entry bootstraps the cluster; the rest join it as additional control planes. Use one, three or five -- an even number cannot form an etcd quorum.

nodeName.title: Host name
nodeName.description: Name of the blade. Must be a valid DNS-1123 label, and becomes the Kubernetes node's name in the cluster.

nodeUuid.title: Ironic node UUID
nodeUuid.description: UUID of an Ironic node that already exists. Leave empty to have Ironic allocate one on first registration.

parentNode.title: Parent node
parentNode.description: UUID or name of a parent Ironic node, for hardware modelled as a child of an enclosure or chassis. Leave empty for a standalone server.

oobIp.description: Address of this node's out-of-band management NIC. Required for a multi-node control plane: etcd binds its peer and client URLs to it, and it is written into the etcd server certificate. Use the management NIC rather than the data NIC, whose DHCP lease changes across reboots and breaks the etcd peer URLs.
oobIp.title: Management NIC address

driver.title: BMC driver
driver.description: Ironic hardware driver for this blade's management controller -- `redfish` where it is available, otherwise `ipmi`.

driver_info.title: BMC connection details
driver_info.description: Driver-specific connection parameters passed to Ironic verbatim: `redfish_address`, `redfish_username`, `redfish_password` and usually `redfish_system_id` for Redfish; the `ipmi_*` equivalents for IPMI.

ports.title: Network ports
ports.description: The blade's NICs, each with an `address` (MAC) and optional `pxe_enabled`. Ironic writes the per-MAC PXE configuration only for ports that exist before the deploy starts, so a blade whose ports are missing PXE-boot-loops. Declare every NIC that can boot.

items.title: Control plane node
items.description: One control plane member. The first entry in the list bootstraps the cluster.

nodes.title: Control plane nodes

node.description: Older single-node form, kept so existing clusters keep working. Ignored when `nodes` is set, which is the form to use.

upgrade.description: Upgrade the control plane to a new Kubernetes version by reimaging, one node at a time.

targetNode.title: Node to upgrade
targetNode.description: Name of the one control plane node to reimage now, so it comes back on the current Kubernetes version. Clear it, or move it on to the next node, once the host reports itself provisioned again. Never name more than one.

upgrade.title: Kubernetes upgrade

recovery.description: Recover a control plane node whose deployment failed or whose hardware was replaced.

undeployMode.title: Cleaning on release
undeployMode.description: What Ironic does between tearing the deployment down and offering the blade again. `full` runs the standard clean steps, including the disk erase. `none` skips cleaning entirely -- seconds instead of hours, with this cluster's data still on disk. Private labs only.

items.title: Control plane node to recover
items.description: A control plane node being released back to Ironic for recovery.

failedNodes.title: Failed control plane nodes
failedNodes.description: Control plane nodes to release back to Ironic. Move an entry here from `nodes` when it is stuck; once Ironic reports it available, move it back into `nodes` -- at any position but the first -- and it rejoins.

recovery.title: Control plane recovery

controlPlane.title: Control plane
controlPlane.description: The cluster's control plane. List one, three or five nodes; the first is the node that bootstraps the cluster and the rest join it.

drainTimeout.description: How long to wait for a removed worker's pods to be evicted before releasing the hardware anyway -- for example 5m.
drainTimeout.title: Drain timeout

nodes.description: Workers to run in this cluster. Add an entry to grow the cluster; a new blade is provisioned and joined on its own.

removed.description: Workers to drain and release. Move an entry here from `nodes`: its pods are evicted, then the blade is released back to Ironic. Delete the entry entirely once Ironic reports the host available, which unregisters it. Removing a worker straight from `nodes` skips the drain.

items.title: Failed worker
items.description: A worker being released without a drain, because it is already unreachable.

failedNodes.description: Workers to release without draining, for a node that is already unreachable and whose pods cannot be evicted.
failedNodes.title: Failed workers

workers.title: Workers
workers.description: The cluster's worker nodes. Each joins once the first control plane has published its join command.

connectorVerbose.description: Log every request and response exchanged with the Ironic API, bodies included, for every blade in this cluster. Without it a rejected call surfaces as a bare status code with Ironic's own explanation discarded. Credential headers are redacted. Verbose -- leave off in normal operation.
connectorVerbose.title: Log the Ironic HTTP exchange

debug.title: Debugging
debug.description: Diagnostic switches. All off by default.

lifecycleApiVersion.description: API version of the bare-metal host composition this cluster renders -- for example composition.krateo.io/v0-6-3. It must match the registered version of the baremetal-host blueprint: registering a new one stops the previous version being served, and a stale value here fails every render. Leave empty to use the version this chart was released against.
lifecycleApiVersion.title: Host API version

install.title: Install the runner
install.description: Put the hydrophone binary on the bootstrapping control plane, with a note next to the output directory explaining how to run it. Installing it does not run anything.

runOnBoot.title: Run the suite on first boot
runOnBoot.description: Run the full conformance suite as soon as the cluster comes up. It takes around two hours and pulls a large image, so leave this off and start it deliberately unless you genuinely want every bring-up to spend that time certifying itself.

outputDir.title: Output directory
outputDir.description: Directory on the node where conformance results are written.

conformance.title: CNCF conformance runner
conformance.description: Install the CNCF conformance test runner onto the node that bootstraps the cluster, so a reimage does not silently take it away again.

nodeAccess.title: Node access
nodeAccess.description: How to reach a provisioned node. Default-safe: with nothing set the `ironic` account is locked and SSH password authentication is off. Password login requires both a password and allowPasswordAuth.

sshAuthorizedKeys.title: SSH authorized keys
sshAuthorizedKeys.description: Public keys added to the `ironic` user. The preferred way in.

items.title: Public key
items.description: One SSH public key, e.g. `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... operator@host`.

password.title: Node password
password.description: Plaintext password for the `ironic` user. Ignored unless Allow password auth is also enabled. Lab use; rotate after.

allowPasswordAuth.title: Allow password auth
allowPasswordAuth.description: Must be enabled AND a password supplied before any password login is rendered into cloud-init.
